Thus both squared lengths are 1, inner product is -1/2, angle is 120 degrees, and alpha+beta=u_1. All six local roots, including negatives, appear exactly once.

diagram_math_checks.checks: Eight endpoints are exactly (+/-1,0),(0,+/-1),(+/-1,+/-1). Alpha is (1,-1), beta is (0,1); squared lengths 2 and 1 and inner product -1 give angle 135 degrees and length ratio sqrt(2). Positive roots alpha,beta,alpha+beta,alpha+2beta are (1,-1),(0,1),(1,0),(1,1), with their four negatives also drawn.

Set alpha=(sqrt(6),0), beta=(-sqrt(6)/2,sqrt(2)/2). Direct dot products give exactly 6,2,-3; hence angle 150 degrees and length ratio sqrt(3). The six unnegated roots alpha,beta,alpha+beta,alpha+2beta,alpha+3beta,2alpha+3beta have polar coordinates (0,sqrt(6)),(150,sqrt(2)),(30,sqrt(2)),(90,sqrt(2)),(120,sqrt(6)),(60,sqrt(6)); their negatives fill the remaining directions. Thus the two foreach loops draw exactly the twelve roots, with six long and six short arrows and correct alpha/beta labels.

All arrows run from the common origin to root endpoints; they are vectors, not graph incidence or morphisms. Each panel uses a uniform Euclidean scale, separately stated in the caption; ratios and angles within each panel are preserved. No new dependency or defining clause is introduced. The original Example, Facts and four verification steps are preserved apart from terminal whitespace; the proof does not use the picture.
